subject: history

provenance.source: AglaSem Docs copy of the NTA master question paper (CUET UG 2026 Question Paper History, 42 PDF pages: a cover plus 41 numbered pages), https://docs.aglasem.com/view/71d24a10-c701-11f1-8cb1-0aa932765c8b, PDF https://cdn.aglasem.com/aglasem-doc/71d24a10-c701-11f1-8cb1-0aa932765c8b/71d24a10-c701-11f1-8cb1-0aa932765c8b.pdf (9,870,409 bytes), downloaded 22 Nov 2026 under the owner's 22 Nov 2026 request for more subjects. English text transcribed from the page images (OCR used as a cross-check). Answers from NTA's CUET (UG) 2026 final answer key (option ids), subject 314.
provenance.keySource: A question is authenticated when its printed NTA question id is in the 24-05-2026 (Second) final key for subject 314 and the key option id is one of its four printed option ids. Printed option ids are consecutive per question.

bankRead: One read-only read on 22 Nov 2026 with the repo read script (SELECT only): 273 visible history rows, of which 259 pass readablePracticeQuestions (equals the 259 in the 21 Nov inventory snapshot; the 14 others are visible but not eligible and are not cited). Served copy: tmp/1122-coverage/snap/history/served_rows.json and served_history.json (eligibility output eligible.txt).
keyCardDeck: data/keycards/decks/history.json (v3, 1587 cards; key_card_suspended was not re-read, the earlier subjects had none suspended)
syllabusSource: Bank chapter names for history; every question sits on the 2026 syllabus (Themes in Indian History I to III).
method: data/coverage/METHOD.md (STRICT rule; doubtful = not covered; Key cards count for theory; an answer readable off a printed passage is skill). Facts written first: tmp/1122-coverage/checkerA-hist/A_facts_before_search.txt. Search: tmp/1122-coverage/checkerA-hist/s.mjs over the served copy and the deck; builder build_A.mjs checks every cited id.
paperStructure: One compulsory History paper of 50 questions: Sub-section 1 = 40 single questions (Q101-140), Sub-section 2 = a comprehension passage on Shah Mal (1857) with 5 questions (Q141-145), Sub-section 3 = a comprehension passage on the Constituent Assembly speech of an Adibasi member with 5 questions (Q146-150). The printed section header says 42 questions, which does not match the 50 ids printed; the key has 50 rows for this shift.

facts: The decadent (Late Harappan) phase of the civilisation is c. 1900 BCE to 1300 BCE

matches.teaches: Early, Mature (2600-1900) and the decadent phase 1900-1300 BCE termed Late Harappan

questions.reason: Key card calls 1900-1300 BCE the decadent phase, the same wording and answer.

facts: Archaeo-botanists are specialists in ancient plant remains

matches.teaches: archaeo-botanists are specialists in ancient plant remains

questions.reason: Key card is the same question and answer.

facts: Terracotta models of the plough have been found at Cholistan and Banawali
questions.reason: The only plough cards say the bull on seals suggests oxen ploughing, and Cholistan appears only as abandoned Mature Harappan sites; no served row or card names Banawali or says plough models were found at Cholistan and Banawali.

facts: John Marshall was the first professional archaeologist to bring experience from Greece and Crete to India

facts: Lower Town at Mohenjodaro provides examples of residential buildings (statement A, true)
no windows in ground-level walls (B, true)
an apparent concern for privacy, so "no concern" is false (C)
every house had its own brick-paved bathroom (D, true)
questions.reason: Cards give the no-windows and privacy point and the brick-paved bathroom in every house, but nothing served says the Lower Town provides examples of residential buildings; the item tests all four statements.

facts: Harappans seem to have believed in the afterlife: pottery and ornaments buried with the dead
questions.reason: Cards say the dead were laid in pits and that jewellery is found in burials of men and women; none says pottery and ornaments were buried in the belief of an afterlife.
